newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta extends Megawati office closure deadline.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta extends Megawati office closure deadline.

text.p: A Jakarta official on Thursday extended a deadline for ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri to close her office, but there was no hint of an easing in government hostility towards her political activities.

Tarto Sudiro, a Megawati supporter and member of parliament, told Reuters a letter addressed to Megawati from East Jakarta Mayor Sudarsono set a new deadline of around 11:30 a.m. (0430 GMT) on Friday.
A judge, meanwhile, adjourned hearings on a lawsuit filed by Megawati against the government, military and political rivals over her June ejection as leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).
Judge I Gde Ketut Sukarata adjourned the suit on Thursday after after the defence questioned the court's jurisdiction.
"The court is adjourned until October 10...when we will hand down a decision on whether this court has the authority to hear this case," the judge said.

Megawati had set up a new office for her faction of the PDI after police raided the official party headquarters on July 27, evicting her supporters and sparking the worst riots in the city of some 10 million people in more than two decades.

The authorities have warned her against continuing her political activities, and the East Jakarta mayor sent a letter late Monday afternoon giving Megawati's faction 72 hours in which to close the office on the grounds that it violated residential zoning laws.
The municipality delivered a letter on Thursday morning setting a new deadline of 24 hours from receipt of the note.

"If you do not implement in a short time what has been ordered, the government of Jakarta represented by the mayor of East Jakarta will implement the closure and you will bear the consequences," the letter said.
Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno, attended a ceremonial meal at the two-storey suburban building hours before the original deadline on Thursday.
She thanked some 250 supporters for attending the meal and said the office was a "temporary" one because she was seeking reinstatement as PDI leader through the courts.
Aides said they were considering what to do next in the light of the latest government move. Earlier, Megawati supporters had said they would defy the order.
Political analysts have said the government wanted her out of the PDI leadership for fear she would draw votes away from the ruling Golkar in general elections at the end of May next year.
The Christian-Nationalist PDI, Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) are the only groups legally entitled to contest the elections.
